summary: The world's clock and weather, which all players' games follow, and questions about the world, such as what a ray hits, the ground under a point, and what stands nearby. The server has no world geometry, so it asks one player's game. Its promise settles with the answer, or without one after five seconds or if that player leaves. Client scripts ask their own game and get the answer within the call, in a frame or two, with more detail on the hit, including kind, mesh, class, name and level GUID. That suits archery, fishing, building, and pressing a key while looking at something. A client's answers are not sent to others and prove nothing to the server.

SHARED_DIMENSION.summary: The shared dimension, 4294967295, where every player starts and everyone sees each other. Dimensions are unsigned 32-bit numbers (0 to 4294967295), so this one does not fit a signed 32-bit database column such as PostgreSQL's INTEGER: store dimensions as BIGINT.
SHARED_DIMENSION.exampleLua:
local World = kcds.world.World
if player.dimension == World.SHARED_DIMENSION then
  print("player " .. tostring(player.id) .. " is in the shared world")
end

landmarks.summary: Points of interest in the server's level, from the game's level files: { name, group, level, position }. `group` is the part of the map the files put it under, and `position` is the middle of what the level places there, not a map marker, so it may be in a tree or on a roof. Empty on a level not in the catalogue.
landmarks.exampleLua:
local first = table.unpack(kcds.world.World.landmarks())
if first then
  print(first.name, first.position.x, first.position.y)
end

replicasAround.summary: Server entities around a point, closest first: players, horses, NPCs, dogs, props, dropped items, doors and stashes, each as its own object. It needs no client, so it is immediate. Gates are not listed, since their catalogue has no positions. For the level's own entities, use a client's entitiesAround.

params.position: The world point to measure from.
params.radius: How far to look, in metres.
params.dimension: Optional: by default the global one, where all bodies start.

replicasAround.example:
const nearby = kcds.world.World.replicasAround({ x: 1200, y: 800, z: 40 }, 25);
console.info(`${nearby.length} things within 25 m`);
replicasAround.exampleLua:
local nearby = kcds.world.World.replicasAround({ x = 1200, y = 800, z = 40 }, 25)
print(tostring(#nearby) .. " things within 25 m")
replicasAround.exampleCs:
var nearby = World.ReplicasAround(new { x = 1200, y = 800, z = 40 }, 25);
Log.Info($"{nearby.Length} things within 25 m");

addInteraction.summary: Adds the game's "press [key] to ..." hint on a level entity by name, on a player's or NPC's body, which that player does not see, on a horse, moving with it, on a resource's Prop, aimed at by its mesh, or at a position. A player aiming at it within `radius` metres sees the hint, and using it runs your handler. It returns an object with setEnabled, setText, setPlayers, where null means everyone, and remove. A resource's interactions end when it stops. Several on one target show together, one per key, as the game shows "E talk, R pickpocket" on its people. A player's game gets at most 255 of the interactions they can see: when there are more, the 255 nearest to them, picked again every second as they move (one on a level entity, whose place the server does not know, comes after those whose place it knows).

params.options: `entity`, a level entity's name, a Player, an Npc, a Horse or a Prop, or `position`; `text`, one line; `radius`, metres, default 2; `key`, an ActionHint key, default 'primary_action', where 'script_action' is KCDS's free key, U; `mode`, 'press' or 'hold', with `holdDuration`, seconds, default 1; `targetRadius` and `targetHeight`, the aimed cylinder for targets with no box, default 0.6 and 1.8.
params.handler: (player, interaction) => void, run when a player uses it.

addInteraction.exampleLua:
local World = kcds.world.World
local Chat = kcds.core.Chat

World.addInteraction({ position = kcds.math.Vector3.new(-2820, -1320, 104), text = "Ring the bell", radius = 3 }, function(ringer) return Chat.sendToAll(tostring(ringer.nickname) .. " rings the bell") end)

-- Two keys on one prisoner's body.
World.addInteraction({ entity = prisoner, text = "Search", key = "primary_action" }, function(searcher)
  Chat.sendToPlayer(searcher, "Nothing on them.")
end)
World.addInteraction({ entity = prisoner, text = "Untie", key = "script_action" }, function(helper)
  Chat.sendToPlayer(helper, "You untie the rope.")
end)

-- A hint on a horse that only its owner sees, wherever it walks.
local feed = World.addInteraction({ entity = horse, text = "Feed", radius = 3 }, function(feeder)
  Chat.sendToPlayer(feeder, "The horse eats.")
end)
feed:setPlayers({ owner })

raycast.summary: Asks a player's game to trace a ray, resolving to { answered, reason, hit }. `hit` is null or { position, normal, distance, terrain, entity, surface, kind, model, category, material, entityGuid, entityName, entityClass, levelObject }. `entity` is the player, NPC or horse hit, or null. `kind` is 'terrain', 'entity', 'vegetation', 'brush' or 'static'. `model` is a brush or vegetation mesh in lower case. `category` is 'tree', 'bush', 'plant' or 'rock'. `levelObject` is what LevelEdit.apply needs to find the object, where a tree, bush or plant the level paints is a 'brush' object found by mesh and position, and it is null for terrain and anything spawned. Its `unseen` is true for a brush its layer hides: an invisible collision of the level's, which a hiding LevelEdit takes the collision of. `material` is currently always null.

params.player: The player whose game traces it, which must show that part of the world.
params.options: `mode`: 'cover', the default, for terrain, buildings and objects, but not living bodies; 'anything', which adds bodies; 'ground', for terrain and static geometry; or 'terrain'.

raycast.exampleLua:
local hit = kcds.world.World.raycast(player, player.position, target, { mode = "cover" }):await().hit
if not hit then
  kcds.core.Chat.sendToPlayer(player, "Clear line of sight")
end

traceAll.summary: Like raycast, but resolves to { answered, reason, hits } with all hits along the ray, nearest first.

params.player: The player whose game traces it.
params.options: `mode` as for raycast, and `max` hits, 1 to 16.

snapToGround.summary: Asks a player's game for the ground's height under a point, resolving to { answered, reason, z, hit }, with z null if there is no ground. The server has no world of its own: with player null, any ready player on the map answers, and with nobody there it resolves with answered false and reason 'no player'. An answer traced from the top (no z given) is kept for ten minutes by half-metre cell, so the same place is known again without asking anyone (reason 'kept').

params.player: The player whose game traces it, or null for any ready player on the map.
params.position: The point; its x and y are used, and z as the height to trace down from (under a bridge or in a cave; such answers are not kept).
params.options: `mode` as for raycast ('ground' or 'terrain'); `map`, one of World.maps, the player's map or the first map by default.

snapToGround.exampleLua:
-- server: the ground under a camp, whoever is online
local ground = kcds.world.World.snapToGround(nil, { x = 512, y = 1800 }):await()
if ground.answered and ground.z ~= nil then
  print("the camp stands at " .. tostring(ground.z) .. " m")
end

entitiesAround.summary: Asks a player's game which replicated bodies it shows around a point, resolving to { answered, reason, entities }, each { entity, position, distance }, nearest first.

levelEntitiesAround.summary: Asks a player's game which entities the level places around a point, such as doors, levers, trigger areas, lights and the items on a drying rack, resolving to { answered, reason, entities }, nearest first. Each is { guid, name, class, position, distance, levelObject }: `guid` is the level's sixteen hex digits, and `levelObject` is what LevelEdit.apply takes to hide or move it. Players' bodies and anything spawned this session are left out. It sees only what that game has streamed in, so ask a player who is near.

params.options: `max`, 1 to 32, default 32: the nearest that many.

levelEntitiesAround.exampleLua:
local World, LevelEdit = kcds.world.World, kcds.world.LevelEdit

-- Hide the sausages on the rack the player stands at.
local around = World.levelEntitiesAround(player, player.position, 3):await()
for _, found in ipairs(around.entities) do
  if string.sub(found.name, 1, 7) == "sausage" and found.levelObject then
    -- the level object as it is, hidden
    local hidden = {}
    for key, value in pairs(found.levelObject) do
      hidden[key] = value
    end
    hidden.hidden = true
    LevelEdit.apply(hidden)
  end
end

day.summary: The world clock's current day, as whole days since it started.

hour.summary: The current hour, from 0 up to 24, with minutes as the fraction.
hour.example:
const { hour } = kcds.world.World;
const night = hour < 5 || hour >= 21;
hour.exampleLua:
local hour = kcds.world.World.hour
local night = hour < 5 or hour >= 21
hour.exampleCs:
var hour = World.Hour;
var night = hour < 5 || hour >= 21;

timeScale.summary: Game seconds per real second, where 0 freezes the clock. Default 15.

weather.summary: The preset the sky shows or is fading to.

lastWeather.summary: The preset the sky is fading from.
lastWeather.exampleLua:
local World = kcds.world.World

if World.weatherFade then
  print("from " .. World.lastWeather .. " to " .. World.weather)
end

weatherFade.summary: Whether the sky is still fading from lastWeather to weather.

weatherLeft.summary: Game seconds left in the fade, or 0 once settled.

rainStrength.exampleLua:
if kcds.world.World.rainStrength > 0.5 then
  kcds.core.Chat.sendToAll("It pours.")
end

snow.summary: The snow every player's game shows (setSnow): amount on surfaces 0 to 10, frost and freezing 0 to 1, and the flakes falling around each player; all 0 when there is none.
snow.exampleLua:
if kcds.world.World.snow.amount > 0 then
  kcds.core.Chat.sendToAll("Snow lies on the land.")
end

rainLevel.summary: How much of the sky rains, 0 to 1.

wind.summary: The wind in metres per second.

windSpeed.summary: The wind's speed in metres per second.
windSpeed.exampleLua:
if kcds.world.World.windSpeed > 15 then
  kcds.core.Chat.sendToAll("A gale is blowing.")
end

wetness.summary: How wet the ground is from rain over time. It dries much more slowly than it soaks.

puddles.summary: How much water stands in puddles, 0 to 1.

setTime.summary: Moves the clock forward to a day and hour. Returns false if either is out of range or that moment has passed.

setHour.summary: Moves the clock to the next time it is this hour, which may be the next day.

setTimeScale.summary: Sets the clock's speed, in game seconds per real second, from 0, frozen, to 200.

setWeather.summary: Fades the sky to a weather preset over some game seconds, up to 21600, where 0 changes it at once. worldWeatherChange follows.

params.preset: The game's preset name, such as 'cloudless_sunny'.
params.seconds: The fade's length in game seconds.

setRain.summary: Sets the rain. Returns false if a value is out of range.

params.amount: How much of the sky rains, 0 to 1, default 1.

setSnow.summary: Sets the snow every player's game shows, with missing parts as 0; {} melts it. Snow lies on everything that faces up (ground, roofs, rocks) and flakes fall around each player. Sent only when it changes, and to every player whose world becomes ready. Returns false if a value is out of range; nothing changes then.

params.snow: { amount, frost, freezing, flakes }: amount on surfaces 0 to 10 (1 a light cover, 10 deep snow), frost 0 to 1, freezing (how frozen surfaces look) 0 to 1, and flakes falling around each player, a whole number 0 to 10000. The cover costs no frame time of its own (the grass it buries is not drawn), but the flakes do: about a tenth of a game's frame rate for 1000 flakes and a quarter for 3000, so keep heavy snowfall short or use up to about 1000.

setSnow.exampleLua:
local World = kcds.world.World

World.setSnow({ amount = 4, frost = 0.5, freezing = 0.3, flakes = 400 })
World.setSnow({})
setSnow.exampleCs:
World.SetSnow(new { amount = 4, frost = 0.5, freezing = 0.3, flakes = 400 });
World.SetSnow(new { });

setWind.summary: Sets the wind in metres per second, with missing components as 0. Returns false for a non-finite value, or wind over 50 m/s.

params.wind: { x, y, z } in metres per second.

groundHeight.summary: Client only. Finds the surface height below a point with a downward trace, so bridges, floors and roofs count, not just terrain. Returns null if nothing is found.

params.position: The point, with the probe centred on its z.
params.options: `up`, default 5, and `down`, default 200: the search range above and below in metres, up to 512 each.

groundHeight.exampleLua:
-- client: find the ground three metres ahead
local pose = kcds.ui.Camera.getPose()
local ahead = kcds.players.LocalPlayer.position:add(pose.forward:mul(3))
local height = kcds.world.World.groundHeight(ahead)
if height ~= nil then
  print("ground at " .. string.format("%.2f", height) .. " m")
end

setPlaceName.summary: Renames a town or place for all current and future players, wherever the game uses its own text: its quest location and settlement. Names inside a sentence, such as a dialogue line, stay as they are. The same name shows in all languages. Returns false for a place the game does not have.

params.place: The id from World.places, such as 'troskovice'.
params.name: 1 to 128 bytes, or null for the game's name.

setPlaceName.exampleLua:
local World = kcds.world.World

World.setPlaceName("troskovice", "Zahradka")
World.setPlaceName("troskovice", null)

places.summary: All named places, as { id, gameName, name }, with gameName the game's English name and name the current one. For World.setPlaceName.
places.exampleLua:
for _, place in ipairs(kcds.world.World.places()) do
  print(place.id, place.name)
end

setLevelItemsEnabled.summary: Turns off or on the items the level places to pick up, such as tankards, tools and shop goods, for all players. When off, all games hide them, including later joiners, and no pick-up is granted. To start with them off, put { "enabled": false } in level-items.json. When on, a picked-up item is gone for everyone, the first in reach gets it, and worldItemPickup can refuse.

params.enabled: True for the level's items, false for none.

removeLevelItems.summary: Removes the items the level places in one spot, such as the bowls by a camp fire or the goods on one stall, for all players including later joiners, and returns a handle whose restore() brings them back. Items of the level whose position lies within `radius` of `position` are hidden in every game, with the pile or stack look the level draws for them, so nobody can pick them up. With `item`, only items of that class go. Places last until restore() or the server restarts; up to 1024 at once.

params.options: { position, radius, item }: `position` is { x, y, z }; `radius` above 0 and up to 100 metres, default 0.5; `item` an item class name or GUID, default every item.

removeLevelItems.exampleLua:
local World = kcds.world.World

-- Clear the apples from a stall for everyone, and put them back an hour later.
local apples = World.removeLevelItems({ position = { x = 1577, y = 2372, z = 26 }, radius = 2, item = "apple" })
setTimeout(function() return apples:restore() end, 60 * 60 * 1000)

levelItemsEnabled.summary: Whether the level's items are on.

level.exampleLua:
if kcds.world.World.level == "kutnohorsko" then
  print("the server runs Kuttenberg")
end

levelTravel.summary: Whether the game's own travel to another map takes players there (playerTravelling). On by default on a server that runs more than one map, and always off on a server with one map.

setLevelTravel.summary: Turns the game's own travel to another map on or off for the whole server. When off, a fast travel to a map's travel point stays an ordinary fast travel, and playerTravelling does not fire. Player.setMap still works. Throws a TypeError for anything but true or false, and a RangeError for true on a server that runs one map.

maps.summary: Every map this server runs, level first. server.json maps adds more, such as ["trosecko", "kutnohorsko"]. Each player is on one map (Player.map) and sees only players and things on that map. Player.setMap moves a player to another map.

raycast.summary: Client only. Traces a segment through this machine's world and returns the first hit, or null, as { position, normal, distance, surface, terrain, kind, model, category, material, entityGuid, entityName, entityClass, entityId, player, levelObject }. `kind` is 'terrain', 'entity' (doors, props, NPCs, players), 'vegetation' (trees, bushes and plants the level paints), 'brush' (walls, houses, rocks and meshes of the level's prefabs) or 'static' (other level geometry, with no model). `model` is a vegetation or brush mesh, a lower-case path with '/'. `category` is 'tree', 'bush', 'plant' or 'rock'. `entityGuid` is the level's sixteen hex digits, or null for terrain, static geometry and anything spawned this session. `player` is whose body it was. `surface` names the material, such as mat_wood or mat_water. `material` is currently always null. `levelObject` is what the level placed, in the form LevelEdit.apply uses on any client, { kind: 'brush' or 'entity', name, guid, class, at, rotation, scale }, to spread into a server definition: LevelEdit.apply({ ...hit.levelObject, hidden: true }). A painted tree, bush or plant is also a 'brush' object, which an edit can hide or move but not turn or resize. It is null for terrain, other static geometry and anything spawned this session.

params.to: The end, above 0 and up to 4096 metres away.
params.options: `mode`: 'cover', the default, for the world, props and doors, but not bodies; 'anything', which adds bodies; or 'ground', only what a player could stand on. `ignoreSelf`, true by default, passes through the local player's body.

raycast.exampleLua:
-- client: what the player looks at, within 4 metres
local Key, Camera = kcds.ui.Key, kcds.ui.Camera

Key.bind("e", function()
  local ray = Camera.rayFromScreen({ range = 4 })
  local hit = ray and kcds.world.World.raycast(ray.origin, ray.target, { mode = "anything" })
  if (hit and hit.entityClass) == "AnimDoor" then
    print("a door: " .. tostring(hit.entityGuid))
  elseif (hit and hit.surface) == "mat_water" then
    print("water: cast the line")
  end
end)

traceAll.summary: Client only. All solid things along the segment, nearest first, each as for World.raycast. The trace continues behind each hit, so it returns both a window and the wall around it.

params.to: The end, above 0 and up to 4096 metres away.
params.options: `mode` and `ignoreSelf` as for World.raycast, and `maxHits`, 1 to 8, default 8.

traceAll.exampleLua:
-- client
local ray = kcds.ui.Camera.rayFromScreen({ range = 50 })
local hits = kcds.world.World.traceAll(ray.origin, ray.target, { mode = "anything", maxHits = 4 })
print(table.concat(hits:map(function(hit) return tostring(hit.kind) .. " " .. string.format("%.1f", hit.distance) .. " m" end), ", "))

snapToGround.summary: Client only. The same probe as World.groundHeight, returning the full hit as for World.raycast, or null. Its normal gives the slope, and its surface gives the ground's material.
snapToGround.exampleLua:
-- client
local ground = kcds.world.World.snapToGround(kcds.players.LocalPlayer.position)
if ground and ground.normal.z < 0.8 then
  print("too steep to build here")
end

entitiesAround.summary: Client only. Entities this machine has inside a sphere, nearest first, as { position, distance, guid, name, class, physicalized, entityId }. `guid` is the level's sixteen hex digits, or null for anything spawned this session. `entityId` is this machine's own value, so store `guid` instead. It sees only what this client has streamed in.

params.options: `class`, limiting it to one engine class, such as 'AnimDoor', 'NPC_NAI' or 'GeomEntity'; `max`, 1 to 64, default 64; `physicalOnly`, default false, limiting it to entities with physics, found through the physics world.

entitiesAround.exampleLua:
-- client
local World = kcds.world.World

local doors = World.entitiesAround(kcds.players.LocalPlayer.position, 10, { class = "AnimDoor" })
for _, door in ipairs(doors) do
  print(door.guid, string.format("%.1f", door.distance))
end
